```
public Set<ValidationMessage> walk(ExecutionContext executionContext, JsonNode node, JsonNode rootNode, String at, boolean shouldValidateSchema) {
    Set<ValidationMessage> validationMessages = new LinkedHashSet<>();
    if (this.applyDefaultsStrategy.shouldApplyArrayDefaults() && node.isArray()) {
        ArrayNode array = ((ArrayNode) (node));
        for (int i = 0; i < Math.min(node.size(), this.tupleSchema.size()); ++i) {
            JsonNode n = node.get(i);
            JsonNode defaultNode = this.tupleSchema.get(i).getSchemaNode().get("default");
            if (n.isNull() && (defaultNode != null)) {
                array.set(i, defaultNode);
                n = defaultNode;
            }
            doWalk(executionContext, validationMessages, i, n, rootNode, at, shouldValidateSchema);
        }
    }
    return validationMessages;
}
```

Potential exceptions:
- NullPointerException if `applyDefaultsStrategy` is null.
- NullPointerException if `tupleSchema` is null.
- NullPointerException if `node` is null (calling node.isArray()).
- ClassCastException if node.isArray() true but node is not actually an ArrayNode (unlikely because isArray returns true for array nodes; but casting to ArrayNode might still be safe; but if node is a subclass not ArrayNode? Usually Jackson's ArrayNode implements isArray true and is castable.)
- NullPointerException if `this.tupleSchema.get(i)` returns null, then calling getSchemaNode() leads NPE.
- NullPointerException if `this.tupleSchema.get(i).getSchemaNode()` returns null (unlikely but possible).
- NullPointerException if `defaultNode` is null? That's fine; they check.
- NullPointerException if `executionContext` is null and doWalk expects non-null? The method passes executionContext to doWalk; if doWalk uses it, could NPE inside doWalk, but not from this method directly.

- IndexOutOfBoundsException? The loop uses Math.min(node.size(), tupleSchema.size()), so safe.

- IllegalArgumentException if node is not array but applyDefaultsStrategy true? The condition prevents casting only when node.isArray() true, so safe.

Thus exception scenarios revolve around null fields.
